results.label: the card is its own section with a title that names both cadences
the card renders both cadences as their own blocks, addressed by kind rather than by position
the totals separate a completed review from a draft, an imported copy, an unreadable row and a period with NO artifact
a saved period is marked as saved and carries the trader’s own focus, not a summary the app invented
a draft says draft and an imported copy says unverified, in the same line as the period it belongs to
a period with no artifact says exactly that, and the card says what it does NOT mean
a period with no closed trade reports NO amount rather than a flat zero, and a close with no recorded amount is counted instead of zeroed
the period still running is labelled as still open rather than counted as a period that was not reviewed
an artifact outside the scanned window is counted on screen instead of disappearing
the card states the two rulers rather than presenting one number as both, and never compares reviewed with unreviewed periods
the card makes no percentage, causal or profit claim the payload did not make
the read-only basis reaches the screen, so a reader is told this is an acknowledgement and not a permission
an unknown record is shown as UNKNOWN, never as a period list of "no artifact recorded"
a payload that never arrived takes the same path: unknown, not a clean record
a reload is offered and it re-reads the same view rather than silently reloading a page whose workspace moved
the reload keeps the workspace/account/session it was rendered under: unchanged, it navigates to the same view and sends no toast
and when the account changed under it, the reload REFUSES with one error toast instead of rendering another desk’s record
the analytics view mounts the card and the page loads it, and the mount sits above the view’s own tabs
and it is mounted after the rule-break card, so the review reads numbers, breaks, then the period record

scope: M13/M65 real DOM: the review-period card the review reads: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
